summary: This script is a Docker container management tool that lets you interactively select running containers using a fuzzy finder (fzf) and then stop or kill them. It shows you detailed information about each container—like its IP address, current resource usage, and mounted volumes—so you can make an informed choice before stopping a container. Depending on whether you press Enter or Ctrl-K, it either gracefully stops or forcefully kills the selected containers.

explanations.4: This calls a helper function to verify that both fzf and docker are installed and available; if either is missing, the script exits early.
explanations.5: This checks if there are any running containers to work with; if not, the script exits cleanly without doing anything.
explanations.7: These are variable declarations that will hold the output from fzf, the key pressed, the container selections, and the command to execute.
explanations.29: This pipes a list of running containers (with ID, name, image, and status) into fzf so the user can select one or more containers.
explanations.30: The `-m` flag allows multi-selection (pick multiple containers at once); `--ansi` enables colored output; `--layout=reverse` puts the selection list at the bottom.
explanations.33: This tells fzf to watch for the Ctrl-K key press as a special action, separate from the default Enter key.
explanations.34: This shows a preview panel on the right side of fzf that displays detailed information about each container as you hover over it.
explanations.39: The first line of fzf's output is the key that was pressed (either Enter or Ctrl-K), so we extract it here.
explanations.41: We skip the first line (which is the key) and extract only the first column (the container ID) from each selected row.
explanations.46: This converts the multi-line string of container IDs into a proper Zsh array so we can pass them safely to the docker command.
explanations.59: This calls a helper function to print the command in a user-friendly way before executing it, using the appropriate color for the action.
explanations.60: This executes the actual docker command (either `docker stop` or `docker kill`) on all selected container IDs.
